dedupe_keys.name: agent based network model of maritime blockage impacts on global supply chains suez canal 2021

description: This agent-based complex network model simulates how a blockage of a maritime chokepoint spreads through global supply chains, integrated with frequently updated maritime data. The authors take the March 2021 Suez Canal blockage as the case, which delayed 432 vessels carrying cargo worth 92.7 billion US dollars. They estimate the trajectories and cargo values of the delayed vessels at second-to-hourly resolution and use an adaptive multi-agent model of cargo blockage and daily supply chain impacts. The blockage led to global losses of about 136.9 billion dollars (127.5 to 147.3), with India bearing 75%, and losses grew nonlinearly with blockage duration, escalating quickly after five days. The article states the model can be applied to other blockage scenarios as an early alert. Its data statement says the AIS data are restricted and licensed, while input-output tables come from Eora26, trade flows from BACI and sea distances from the CERDI database. Access: open article on PubMed Central (2024). Licence and cost: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, free to read. Caveats: no code release is named, and vessel data are proprietary. It supports agent-based, cascading failure and resilience studies of chokepoints. It relates to the Eora2 and BACI data, the ADB passageway transit data and the Verschuur port supply chain data in the catalogue.
